notes.summary: This chapter extends the trigonometric ratios from acute angles to all real numbers, using radian measure and the unit circle, and then builds the compound-angle, multiple-angle and sum–product identities. CBSE asks for degree–radian conversions, arc-length problems, signs and values at large or negative angles, and evaluations or proofs using the identities.
keyPoints: π radians = 180°. So 1° = π/180 rad ≈ 0.01746 rad, and 1 rad = 180°/π ≈ 57°16′ (with π = 22/7). Arc length l = rθ, with θ in radians.
Signs by quadrant: in I all ratios are positive; in II only sin and cosec; in III only tan and cot; in IV only cos and sec (All–Sin–Tan–Cos).

Domain and range: sin and cos have domain R and range [−1, 1]. tan has domain R − {(2n + 1)π/2} and range R. cosec has domain R − {nπ} and range (−∞, −1] ∪ [1, ∞). sec has the same range as cosec, with domain R − {(2n + 1)π/2}.
Periods: sin, cos, sec and cosec repeat every 2π; tan and cot repeat every π. Even or odd: cos(−x) = cos x, while sin(−x) = −sin x and tan(−x) = −tan x.
Allied angles: sin(π − x) = sin x, cos(π − x) = −cos x, sin(π/2 + x) = cos x and cos(π/2 + x) = −sin x.
Compound angles: sin(x ± y) = sin x cos y ± cos x sin y; cos(x ± y) = cos x cos y ∓ sin x sin y; tan(x ± y) = (tan x ± tan y)/(1 ∓ tan x tan y).

Double and triple angles: sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x = 2 tan x/(1 + tan²x); cos 2x = cos²x − sin²x = 2cos²x − 1 = 1 − 2sin²x; tan 2x = 2 tan x/(1 − tan²x); sin 3x = 3 sin x − 4 sin³x; cos 3x = 4cos³x − 3 cos x; tan 3x = (3 tan x − tan³x)/(1 − 3tan²x).

Sum to product: sin C + sin D = 2 sin((C + D)/2) cos((C − D)/2); sin C − sin D = 2 cos((C + D)/2) sin((C − D)/2); cos C + cos D = 2 cos((C + D)/2) cos((C − D)/2); cos C − cos D = −2 sin((C + D)/2) sin((C − D)/2).
Product to sum: 2 sin x cos y = sin(x + y) + sin(x − y); 2 cos x cos y = cos(x + y) + cos(x − y); 2 sin x sin y = cos(x − y) − cos(x + y).
traps: Using degrees in l = rθ. The angle must be in radians.
Getting the sign wrong after reducing a large or negative angle. Fix the quadrant first, then decide the sign.
Sign slips in cos C − cos D, which has a leading minus, and in cos(x + y), which has a minus between its terms.
Writing sin 3x = 3 sin x + 4 sin³x or cos 3x = 3 cos x − 4 cos³x. The correct forms are 3 sin x − 4 sin³x and 4cos³x − 3 cos x.
Automatically taking the positive root when finding one ratio from another. The quadrant decides the sign.
notes.examTip: Reduce any large or negative angle using the period first (360° for sin and cos, 180° for tan), then apply the quadrant sign before using a standard value.

questions.text: Taking π = 22/7, one radian is approximately equal to:
questions.explanation: π radians = 180°, so 1 radian = 180°/π. With π = 22/7, this is 180 × 7/22 = 1260/22 ≈ 57.27°. The decimal part is 0.27° × 60 ≈ 16′, so 1 radian ≈ 57°16′. Note that 180° is π radians, not 1 radian. So the answer is 57°16′.

questions.text: Which of the following trigonometric functions is an even function, that is, f(−x) = f(x) for every x in its domain?
questions.explanation: On the unit circle, the angle −x gives the point (cos x, −sin x). So cos(−x) = cos x, while sin(−x) = −sin x. It follows that tan(−x) = −tan x and cosec(−x) = −cosec x, so these three are odd functions. Only cos x (and sec x) is even. So the answer is cos x.

questions.text: The domain of the function y = tan x is:
questions.explanation: tan x = sin x / cos x, so it is defined only where cos x ≠ 0. cos x = 0 at x = ±π/2, ±3π/2 and so on, the odd multiples of π/2, that is, x = (2n + 1)π/2. R − {nπ} is the domain of cot x and cosec x, which need sin x ≠ 0. So the domain of tan x is R − {(2n + 1)π/2 : n ∈ Z}.

30′ = 30/60 of a degree = 1/2°, so 47°30′ = 47.5° = 95/2 degrees. Radian measure = (π/180) × degree measure = (π/180) × (95/2) = 95π/360. Dividing top and bottom by 5 gives 19π/72. Keeping the minus sign, −47°30′ = −19π/72 radian.

questions.text: The minute hand of a watch is 2.1 cm long. How far does its tip move in 20 minutes? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: The minute hand turns 360° in 60 minutes, so in 20 minutes it turns 120° = 120 × π/180 = 2π/3 radian. Arc length l = rθ = 2.1 × 2π/3 = 1.4π. With π = 22/7, l = 1.4 × 22/7 = 4.4 cm. For comparison, 13.2 cm is the whole circumference. So the tip moves 4.4 cm.

tan is an odd function, so tan(−585°) = −tan 585°. tan has period 180°, so tan 585° = tan(585° − 3 × 180°) = tan 45° = 1. So tan(−585°) = −1. Check another way: −585° + 720° = 135°, and tan 135° = −1.

questions.text: If cot x = −5/12 and x lies in the second quadrant, then sec x equals:
questions.explanation: cosec²x = 1 + cot²x = 1 + 25/144 = 169/144, so cosec x = ±13/12. In the second quadrant sin x > 0, so cosec x = 13/12 and sin x = 12/13. Then cos x = cot x × sin x = (−5/12)(12/13) = −5/13, which is negative as expected in quadrant II. So sec x = 1/cos x = −13/5.

questions.text: If tan x = 1/2, then the value of tan 2x is:
questions.explanation: Use tan 2x = 2 tan x / (1 − tan²x). The numerator is 2 × 1/2 = 1. The denominator is 1 − 1/4 = 3/4. So tan 2x = 1 ÷ 3/4 = 4/3. The option 4/5 is sin 2x = 2 tan x/(1 + tan²x), and 1 comes from simply doubling tan x.

questions.text: If sin x = 1/3, then the value of sin 3x is:
questions.explanation: Use sin 3x = 3 sin x − 4 sin³x. First, 3 sin x = 3 × 1/3 = 1. Next, 4 sin³x = 4 × 1/27 = 4/27. So sin 3x = 1 − 4/27 = 23/27. The option 31/27 comes from using + instead of −; it is greater than 1, which is impossible for a sine.

questions.text: The value of (sin 75° − sin 15°) / (cos 75° + cos 15°) is:
questions.explanation: By sin C − sin D = 2 cos((C + D)/2) sin((C − D)/2), the numerator is 2 cos 45° sin 30°. By cos C + cos D = 2 cos((C + D)/2) cos((C − D)/2), the denominator is 2 cos 45° cos 30°. Dividing, the factor 2 cos 45° cancels, leaving sin 30°/cos 30° = tan 30° = 1/√3.

questions.text: The value of cos 20° cos 40° cos 80° is:
questions.explanation: Since 2 cos 20° cos 40° = cos 60° + cos 20°, we get cos 20° cos 40° = (1/2)(1/2 + cos 20°). Multiplying by cos 80° gives (1/2)[(1/2)cos 80° + cos 20° cos 80°]. Now cos 20° cos 80° = (1/2)(cos 100° + cos 60°) = (1/2)(−cos 80° + 1/2) = −(1/2)cos 80° + 1/4. So the bracket is (1/2)cos 80° − (1/2)cos 80° + 1/4 = 1/4, and the product is (1/2)(1/4) = 1/8. For comparison, √3/8 is the value of sin 20° sin 40° sin 80°.
